headline_marked: Meta debuts [[cheaper smart glasses]] starting at $299
headline: Meta debuts cheaper smart glasses starting at $299
summary: Meta Glasses come with a camera, speakers, and 8+ hours of battery life
details: Meta has launched a new line of smart glasses, dubbed Meta Glasses, starting at $299. These glasses are being made in partnership with EssilorLuxottica and come in several countries starting today in a variety of color and lens combinations.

The Meta Glasses don't have a screen, but they come with a camera and personal speakers. There's a dedicated button that by default triggers the Meta AI assistant, or you can customize the button to launch a specific feature.

The glasses have over eight hours of battery life, and the on-the-go charging case provides up to 40 hours of additional usage. The Meta AI assistant on these new glasses can answer questions about everything from sports scores to local restaurant picks, can understand what you're seeing, and can help manage your daily life.

The first pair of the new glasses, called the 'Meta Adventurer,' features a rectangular shape, and is available in standard and large sizes. The 'Meta Fury' frame is boxier, resembling popular styles of men's glasses. The most notable are 'Meta Glasses by Kylie,' which feature a slim oval frame designed in collaboration with American model Kylie Jenner.

headline_marked: Transformer Decoders Generate Text [[One Token at a Time]] with Causal Masking
headline: Transformer Decoders Generate Text One Token at a Time with Causal Masking
summary: Learn how Transformer Decoders work, from causal masking to decoding strategies.
details: A Transformer Decoder generates text by predicting one token at a time, using a combination of masked self-attention, cross-attention, and a feed-forward network.
The decoder uses causal masking to only look at previous tokens, preventing it from seeing future answers during training.
The LM Head converts the decoder's representations into vocabulary scores, which are then used to select the next token.
caption:
How do Transformer Decoders generate text?

A Transformer Decoder generates text by predicting one token at a time, using a combination of masked self-attention, cross-attention, and a feed-forward network.

The decoder uses causal masking to only look at previous tokens, preventing it from seeing future answers during training.

The LM Head converts the decoder's representations into vocabulary scores, which are then used to select the next token.
